data.description:
## The gap

`AGENTS.md:256` bans `git stash` in the TICKET STORE only. The code repo has no rule — and this
machine currently carries **130 linked worktrees sharing one stash stack**, with concurrent agents
working in them.

`docs/concurrency.md` §"Why `git stash` in particular is banned there" already documents the hazard
correctly. `src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py` (`_stash_create`, ~L62-146) already migrated push
recovery from `stash push`/`pop` to `stash create` + `apply <sha>` after a real incident that wedged
the store. **The project reached the right conclusion once and only half-applied it.**

## THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE CURRENT SUBSTITUTE

**`git stash create` silently does NOT capture untracked files — and `git stash create -u` accepts
the flag and still does not.** Verified empirically on git 2.55: the `-u` stash commit has only two
parents (no untracked-files parent), and applying it restored only the tracked modification.

That matters because rebar presents `stash create` as the safe substitute, and because a **held-out
TDD oracle is typically a NEWLY AUTHORED, UNTRACKED test file**. For that case `stash create` is a
silent-data-loss trap. The three stashes live on this machine right now happen to be tracked-file
modifications, so they would have survived — the next new test file would not.

## The hazard is generated BY INSTRUCTION

`~/.claude/skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md:261` says "(stash/relocate them…)" and
`~/.claude/skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md:769` says "(stash/save it aside)". Agents following the
documented held-out-oracle discipline are told to stash. **This is the root cause, and it lives
outside this repository** — the skill files are the operator's, so the fix there is theirs to make.
Recorded here so the two halves are not solved independently.

## What the wider evidence says

- **Git upstream has never addressed it.** `git-worktree(1)`'s REFS section lists exactly three
  non-shared exceptions (`refs/bisect`, `refs/worktree`, `refs/rewritten`); `refs/stash` is shared
  **by omission**, and neither `git-stash(1)` nor `git-worktree(1)` nor `gitfaq` warns about it. One
  RFC exists — "stash: let the stash stack live in a configurable ref", 2026-08-23, motivated
  explicitly by AI-agent worktree fleets — **no patch, no consensus, unmerged**.
- **A wrapper banning `git stash` is incomplete**: `git rebase --autostash` writes `refs/stash`
  directly.
- **Flagship OSS projects have no policy** — zero hits across git, Linux, Rust, Node.js, LLVM,
  Kubernetes, Chromium/depot_tools, Homebrew.
- **The convention that DOES exist is in agent tooling and is converging**: microsoft/mcp's
  `AGENTS.md` bans it and prescribes `git diff <ref>` or a throwaway worktree; LibreChat's
  `CLAUDE.md` prefers a WIP commit, or `stash push -m <tag>` + `apply` that specific entry.
  `github/copilot-cli#1725` is an open, unanswered bug against a first-party agent product.

## The substitute for a held-out oracle specifically

**Move the file out of the worktree** — `mv <test> "$(git rev-parse --git-path heldout)/"` and move
it back to validate. Zero git involvement, so zero shared-ref surface; works identically for tracked
and untracked files; trivially reversible. Using `git rev-parse --git-path` rather than `/tmp` keeps
it per-worktree and auto-cleaned with the worktree.

The requirement is that the oracle be **absent from the filesystem** — which a move does directly
and stash only incidentally.

(Runner-up: `git hash-object -w` then `git cat-file -p <sha> > <file>`, round-trip verified. Handles
untracked files, but the loose blob is collectable by `git gc --prune=now` in ANY worktree unless
anchored under a per-worktree ref.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - The `git stash` ban in `AGENTS.md` is generalised from the ticket store to the whole
      repository, in one sentence, pointing at the existing `docs/concurrency.md` passage rather
      than restating its argument.
- [ ] AC2 - The untracked-files caveat is recorded where `stash create` is presented as the safe
      substitute. `stash create` is correct for the tracked-file push-recovery case it was adopted
      for, and unsafe for a new file — both halves must be stated, or the next reader will apply it
      to the wrong case.
- [ ] AC3 - The guidance names the substitute for the held-out-oracle case concretely (move the file
      under `git rev-parse --git-path`), not merely "do not stash".
- [ ] AC4 - `push_recovery.py`'s use of `stash create` is audited against AC2: confirm it only ever
      handles tracked modifications, or fix it. Record which.

## Explicitly NOT doing: a hook or CI gate

A CI gate **cannot see a stash** — it is local, ephemeral state that never reaches a commit. The
only enforcement point is a client-side PreToolUse hook, which is per-machine config rather than
repo-enforceable, and which `--autostash` defeats anyway. The `mechanism-delta` ratchet would
require a `mechanism-ok:` justification for a new `ci_gate` and that justification is weak.

`AGENTS.md` is loaded at launch on every agent session — the same enforcement surface, at none of
the mechanism cost. Revisit only if a stash collision actually loses work here AFTER this guidance
lands; that would be the evidence a mechanism needs, and it is the standard this project already
applies to its other ratchets.
data.title: The git stash ban is scoped to the ticket store only, while 130 linked worktrees share one stack — and the documented substitute, stash create, silently drops untracked files, which is exactly what a held-out oracle usually is
